In a remarkable story of courage and determination, Swedish chemistry professor Charlotta Turner helped rescue her graduate student Firas Jumaah and his family from the clutches of ISIS in Iraq in 2014.

Jumaah, who had initially stayed behind to complete his lab work, immediately returned to Iraq to be with his family.

However, as the situation worsened, Jumaah's family found themselves in grave danger. ISIS conducted a deadly offensive in northern Iraq, massacring and enslaving thousands of Yazidis, including Jumaah's family. With borders closed and the airport inaccessible, Jumaah and his family were forced to go into hiding in a disused bleach factory.

Professor Turner, who had been Jumaah's supervisor, received a text message from him, stating that he would not be able to complete his thesis if he didn't return to Sweden within a week. Moved by Jumaah's desperation, Turner contacted the university's security chief, Per Gustafson, who arranged for a rescue operation.

Over a few days of intense activity, Gustafson hired a security company, which then arranged for a rescue operation. Two Landcruisers carrying four heavily-armed mercenaries roared into the area where Jumaah was hiding, and sped him away to Erbil Airport, along with his wife and two small children.

Jumaah and his family were eventually reunited in Sweden, where Jumaah completed his PhD and now works for a pharmaceutical company in Malmö. The family has almost paid back the university for the rescue operation.

Professor Turner's actions were hailed as a remarkable example of academic solidarity and humanitarianism. "It was almost as if he'd been waiting for this kind of mission," Turner said of Gustafson. "Per Gustafson said that we had a transport and security deal which stretched over the whole world."

This extraordinary story highlights the bravery and selflessness of Professor Turner and the university's security team, who risked their lives to rescue Jumaah and his family from the clutches of ISIS.
